facts.text: Its EcoCenter was certified LEED Platinum by the U.S. Green Building Council in 2013.
The EcoCenter runs off the grid with solar power and a living roof.
facts.note: Off-grid solar and living roof confirmed on sfrecpark EcoCenter pages (1197/1226).

facts.text: Its Nature Exploration Area won UNICEF's 2021 Cities Inspires Award.
A waterfront park of about 7 acres next to the Pier 70 shipyard.
Plans include restoration of historic cranes and a human-powered boating facility.
Casual sibling of Quince, run by Michael and Lindsay Tusk.
Pastas include agnolotti del plin stuffed with rabbit, veal and pork.
The dining room has exposed brickwork and a copper counter and bar.
Covered by a stained glass dome with more than 70,000 pieces of colored glass.
The Palace Hotel opened on its present site on December 19, 1909.
A 4.5-acre park on land once used by Embarcadero Freeway ramps.
Named for civic activist and Supervisor Sue Bierman, a leader of the Freeway Revolt.
facts.note: Name and civic activist/Supervisor confirmed; Freeway Revolt role stated on the Sue Bierman article.

facts.text: Designed by Willis Polk and built in 1917; considered the first U.S. glass curtain-wall building.
facts.note: Wikipedia says it is one of the country's first glass curtain walls (predated by a 1909 Kansas City building), and opened 1918 (built 1917-1918); not "the first".

facts.text: Named for cable car pioneer Andrew Smith Hallidie.
Founded in 1962 by Pat Ramseyer and Nancy White, it began in Oakland.
Moved to Bernal Heights in 1977 and bought an 1890s Italianate-style building.
Named after the 1962 film Walk on the Wild Side.
Chef and owner Greg Lutes opened the restaurant in 2015.
The menu is seasonal and hyper-local, with French, Italian and Asian leanings.
Serves Japanese and Thai noodles, including khao soi and ramen.
Its tonkotsu ramen is flavored with roasted black garlic oil.
A multi-roaster cafe founded by JoEllen Depakakibo.
Opened in 2014 on Cortland Avenue in Bernal Heights.
Describes itself as a hard working coffee joint in love with its neighborhood.
Its store blends coffee and moto culture, inspired by engines and espresso.
Has served Italian and seafood dishes at Fisherman's Wharf since 1997.
Owned by fifth-generation native San Franciscans.
Established in 1973 on Mission Street between 24th and 25th.
Named one of America's Classics by the James Beard Foundation in 2017.
Serves Mission-style burritos whose recipes do not include rice.
Opened in 2014 by chef-owner Pim Techamuanvivit.
Received a Michelin star in 2015, a year after opening.
Holds one Michelin star in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide USA.
The name honors the grandparents of co-owners Ollie Liedags and Rachel Sillcocks.
Serves a surprise tasting menu with brunch-focused cooking.
Began in 2009 as an underground restaurant in chef David Barzelay's apartment.
Moved to its current Mission District location in 2014.
Holds two Michelin stars.
Holds three Michelin stars in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide USA.
facts.note: Quince Michelin restaurant page not returned; other michelin.com pages say three stars in 2026 guide.

facts.text: Founded in 2003 and run by Michael and Lindsay Tusk.
Serves nightly-changing tasting menus built on a partnership with Fresh Run Farm in Bolinas.
The building dates to 1919 and was a winery and cigar store during Prohibition.
Opened as Sotto Mare Oysteria & Seafood on March 17, 2007.
The Azzolino family bought the restaurant in 2014.
Has held one Michelin star for nine consecutive years.
Housed in a landmark building that once held the Four Seas and Hang Far Low restaurants.
Opened in 2015 as the second restaurant from chef-owner Melissa Perello.
Was awarded a Michelin star within its first year of business.
